source_text: Mani apostolus Iesu Christi filiae Menoch. Gratia tibi et salus a Deo nostro, qui est re vera verus Deus, tribuatur ipseque tuam mentem illustret et iustitiam suam tibimet revelet, quia es divinae stirpis fructus. Et post pauca: Per quos et tu splendida - inquit - reddita es agnoscendo, qualiter prius fueris, ex quo genere animarum emanaveris, quod est confusum omnibus corporibus et saporibus et speciebus variis cohaeret. Nam sicut animae gignuntur ab animabus, ita figmentum corporis a corporis natura digeritur. " Quod, ergo, nascitur de carne, caro est et, quod de spiritu, spiritus est " [n209] ; spiritum autem animam intellege, anima de anima, caro de carne [n210] .
pass_a_gloss: Mani apostle of Jesus Christ to the daughter Menoch. Grace to you and salvation from our God, who is in truth the true God, be attributed, and may he himself illuminate your mind and reveal his justice to you, because you are a fruit of divine stock. And after a few: Through whom you also, he says, have been rendered splendid by recognizing of what sort you were before, from which kind of souls you have emanated, which is confused with all bodies and coheres with flavors and various species. For as souls are generated from souls, so the figment of the body is digested from the nature of the body. What therefore is born from flesh is flesh, and what from spirit is spirit; but understand spirit the soul, soul from soul, flesh from flesh.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: ‘Mani, apostle of Jesus Christ, to his daughter Menoch. May grace and salvation be given you from our God, who truly is the true God. May he enlighten your mind and reveal his justice to you, because you are a fruit of divine stock.’ A little later: ‘Through them you too have been made radiant by recognizing what you were before and from what kind of souls you flowed—a kind mixed with all bodies and attached to flavors and various forms. For just as souls are generated from souls, so the body’s formation is drawn from bodily nature. Therefore, “What is born of flesh is flesh, and what is born of spirit is spirit” (John 3:6). Understand spirit, however, to mean soul: soul from soul, flesh from flesh.’

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
